Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year was Kepler's Supernova discovered?
Kepler's Supernova: SN 1604, also known as Kepler's Supernova, Kepler's Nova or Kepler's Star, was a Type Ia supernova that occurred in the Milky Way, in the constellation Ophiuchus.
PHP: Rasmus Lerdorf. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Which company manufactures KAI KF-21 Boramae?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: Korea Aerospace Industries. The KAI KF-21 Boramae (Korean: KF-21 보라매; lit. 'KF-21 Hunting Hawk'; formerly KF-X; commonly KF-21) is a South Korean twin-engine fighter aircraft.
Fufu: Ghana. Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine.
Who is credited with discovering Tennessine?
Tennessine: Yuri Oganessian. Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Who is credited with discovering Ammonia?
Ammonia: Joseph Priestley. Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Who is credited with discovering Selenium?
Selenium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
These large seabirds of the tubenose order range widely across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific, but are notably absent from the North Atlantic today. What birds are they?
Albatross are large seabirds related to the procellariids, storm petrels, and diving petrels in the order Procellariiformes (the tubenoses).
Closely related to Hepatica and Pulsatilla, which flowering plant genus in the buttercup family is nicknamed the windflower?
Anemone is a genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Marketed early on as the Debonair in its conventional-tail form, this piston single has been built continuously longer than any other aircraft ever made — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza is an American general aviation aircraft introduced in 1947 by Beech Aircraft Corporation of Wichita, Kansas.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
This basic unit of digital information most often consists of eight bits, and is called an 'octet' in network protocol documents to avoid ambiguity. What is it?
Byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.
A flightless ratite native to the tropical forests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this large bird has three living species and lacks a keel on its breastbone — name the bird?
Cassowary (Tok) are flightless birds of the genus Casuarius, in the order Casuariiformes.

A long-term lung condition that makes breathing progressively harder due to damaged airways and lung tissue, this condition develops gradually and currently cannot be cured, though treatments and lifestyle changes help manage symptoms. What is this disease, commonly abbreviated?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a long-term lung condition that makes it progressively harder to breathe.
This group of mostly evergreen, cone-bearing trees and shrubs reproduces via wind-pollination, with the seeds themselves also scattered by the wind — what plant group is it?
Conifer are a group of vascular plants and a subset of gymnosperms.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element with atomic number 110 sits below platinum on the periodic table — what's it called?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'female dragon,' and this genus of roughly 200 tree and shrub species now also includes what was once classified as Sansevieria — which genus is it?
Dracaena (plant) is a genus of about 200-220 species of trees and woody shrubs.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.

Heterotrophs like animals, members of this kingdom eat by secreting enzymes into their surroundings, and they get around mainly by simply growing — except for the occasional flagellated spore drifting through air or water. What group is it?
Fungus (pl.: fungi or funguses) is any member of the group of eukaryotic organisms that includes yeasts, molds, as well as mushrooms.
The largest living primate, with arm spans reaching 2.6 metres, this equatorial-African great ape shares up to 99% of its DNA with humans — what is it?
Gorilla are large, primarily herbivorous, great apes that live in the tropical forests of equatorial Africa.
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
Behaviorally and physically dog-like despite being closer kin to felines, this carnivoran's family is the fifth-smallest in its order with only four extant species — what is it?
Hyena (hi-; from Ancient Greek, haina) are feliform carnivoran mammals belonging to the family Hyaenidae (Latin).

Also known by the old names green vitriol and copperas, this heptahydrate salt dissolves in water to form a paramagnetic, octahedral aquo complex and is used medically to fight anemia — which compound is it?
Iron(II) sulfate (British) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4xH2O.

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.

This genus of rod-shaped, gram-positive bacteria forms a significant part of the human microbiota in places like the digestive and genital tracts, and until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul included 261 distinct species — what's the genus?
Lactobacillus is a genus of gram-positive bacteria within the Lactobacillaceae family.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Nicknamed "quicksilver," this is the only metallic element that stays liquid at room temperature, and it's often mined as the red mineral cinnabar — which element is it?
Mercury (element) is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors grow more frequent through reinforcement or fade through punishment and extinction — what is it called?
Operant conditioning is a learning process in which voluntary behaviors are modified by association with the addition (or removal) of reward or aversive stimuli.
A physician in this medical field — devoted to the study of disease and diagnosing it largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — is called a pathologist. What is the field?
Pathology is the study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
This branch of linguistics is concerned with how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived by listeners — name the field?
Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.
Born Joseph Ratzinger in Bavaria, this pontiff led the Catholic Church from 2005 until an unusual resignation in 2013, after which he adopted an 'emeritus' title — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI (born Joseph Alois Ratzinger; 16 April 1927 - 31 December 2022) was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 2005 until his resignation in 2013.
Found in nucleic acids as the building block behind adenine and guanine, this nitrogen-rich heterocyclic compound is the most common of its kind in nature — what is it?
Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of two rings (pyrimidine and imidazole) fused together.
Home to about 200 species — among them the plants we call currants and gooseberries — this genus is the sole member of its own plant family — which genus?
Ribes is a genus of approximately 200 known species of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.

This volatile, colorless, and odorless nerve agent is so potent a chemical weapon that inhaling a lethal dose can cause death from respiratory paralysis within one to ten minutes — what's the compound called?
Sarin (NATO designation GB short for G-series, B) is an extremely toxic organophosphorus compound that has been often used as a chemical weapon due to its extreme potency as a nerve agent.

Built for the Marine Corps by adding a third engine and a seventh main rotor blade to an earlier heavy-lift helicopter, this aircraft entered service in 1981 and flies from Navy ships — which helicopter?
Sikorsky CH-53E Super Stallion is a heavy lift helicopter operated by the United States military.
Members of the family Sciuridae, whose closest living relatives are surprisingly the mountain beaver and dormice, these rodents are native to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa — what are they called?
Squirrel (z)) are members of the family Sciuridae (sih-, -dee), a family that includes small or medium-sized rodents.

A leguminous tree bearing edible brown pod-like fruits with sweet, tangy pulp, indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia, its wood and seed oil have varied uses from cuisine to traditional medicine. What is this tree?
Tamarind (Tamarindus indica) is a leguminous tree bearing edible fruit that is indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
Nicknamed carbamide, this is the simplest amide of carbamic acid: two amino groups joined by a single carbonyl, and the body's chief way of shedding nitrogen in urine. What compound is it?
Urea (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
He co-developed the V-2 at Peenemünde — the first artificial object to cross the Kármán line into space — before bringing his rocketry to the United States; who was this engineer?
Wernher von Braun (23 March 1912 - 16 June 1977) was a German American aerospace engineer and space architect.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
This inflammatory condition causes right lower abdominal pain and is commonly triggered by a blockage from a calcified mass of feces called a fecalith — what is it?
Known medically as tinea pedis, this common fungal infection often begins between the toes and spreads in places like swimming pools and locker rooms — what is it?
Athlete's foot: Skin infection caused by fungus.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Patented in 1976 and sold under the brand name Zebeta, this beta-1-selective medication treats high blood pressure and heart failure — what is it?
Bisoprolol: Beta-1 selective adrenenergic blocker medication used to treat cardiovascular diseases.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
The largest living rodent, this semiaquatic South American grass-grazer lives in sociable herds of 10 to 20 — sometimes up to a hundred — near rivers and ponds; what is it?
A Turkish geologist honored by academies from the US to Russia to Serbia, he received the Gustav-Steinmann-Medaille, geology's top German prize. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör: Turkish scientist, geologist. Ali Mehmet Celâl Şengör (Turkish: [ˈali ˈmehmet ˈdʒeɫal ˈʃænɟœɾ]; born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
A shrub-like bush of western South America with oval leaves and small red berries, its leaves are chewed or brewed as a mild stimulant and famously contain a notorious alkaloid — which plant is it?
Coca: Plant in the Erythroxylaceae family.
This miniature Belgian-French dog breed comes in two varieties named for a butterfly and a moth, based on whether their ears stand erect or hang down — which breed?
Continental Toy Spaniel: Belgian and French breed of dog. The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
First flown in 1938 and built almost 14,000 strong at a factory in Buffalo, New York, this WWII fighter-bomber was known to British and Soviet pilots as the Tomahawk or Kittyhawk — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: American WWII fighter. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.

Known mainly through DNA evidence rather than plentiful fossils, this extinct archaic human group ranged across Asia until about 32,000 years ago, and DNA analysis confirmed the Harbin skull belonged to it — what group is it?
Denisovan: Archaic human species from Asia.
In 1949, this NASA mathematician became the first African-American woman to supervise a team at Langley, later teaching herself and her staff the Fortran language — who is she?
Dorothy Vaughan: American human computer and computer programmer (1910–2008)
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
This system of rules governing clauses, phrases, and word use is often absorbed unconsciously in childhood, long before anyone studies its syntax formally — what field?
Grammar: Structural rules of a language.

Marketed under a well-known brand name, this typical antipsychotic treats everything from schizophrenia to Tourette tics, but carries risks of tardive dyskinesia and dangerous QT-interval prolongation — what drug is it?
Haloperidol: Typical antipsychotic medication. Haloperidol, sold under the brand name Haldol among others, is a typical antipsychotic medication.
Named after the 19th-century physicist who proved electromagnetic waves exist, which SI unit measures one cycle per second?
Hertz: SI unit of frequency. The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
This condition involves a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid around the brain, causing headaches, vision problems, and in babies a rapidly enlarging head — what is it?
Hydrocephalus: Abnormal increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.

The New York Times once called him "the nation's most influential evangelical leader," yet he was never an ordained minister — instead this psychologist founded Focus on the Family and led it from 1977 to 2010. Who was he?
James Dobson: American evangelical Christian psychologist and author (1936–2025)
This Hungarian-American polymath helped build the mathematical framework of quantum physics and codified ideas from game theory to cellular automata — who was he?
John von Neumann: Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957)
This Gram-negative rod bacterium can turn deadly if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brownish-yellow jelly-like sputum — which pathogen?
Klebsiella pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, then drafted the letter Einstein signed that launched the Manhattan Project — who was he?
Leo Szilard: Hungarian-American physicist and inventor (1898–1964)

A four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft, this American plane is a comprehensive update of an older transport design, with over 500 delivered to 26 operators worldwide as of 2022. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules: Military transport aircraft. The C-130J is a comprehensive update of the Lockheed C-130 Hercules, with new engines, flight deck, and other systems.
This is the common name for the larva of flies like houseflies and blowflies — though, confusingly, not for baby mosquitoes — what is it called?
This biological term covers the pairing of organisms for sexual reproduction, encompassing everything from copulation to external fertilization in fish and amphibians — what is it?
Mating: Process of pairing in biology.
Once made by roasting wood — hence its old name 'wood alcohol' — this simplest alcohol smells much like the drinkable kind but is far more poisonous. What is it?
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
Despite its name, this blister-agent chemical weapon isn't always gaseous, and to this day there is no antidote for exposure to it — what is it?
Mustard gas: Chemical warfare agent. There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, from epilepsy and stroke to Parkinson's disease — which field?
Neurology: Medical specialty dealing with disorders of the nervous system.
Named for a discredited belief that it 'rows' itself with its pelvic fins, this family of long pelagic fish includes the longest bony fish alive at up to 8 meters?
Oarfish: Pelagic lampriform fish belonging to Regalecidae.
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this measure comes in an avoirdupois version equal to 1/16 of a pound and a heavier troy version used for precious metals — what unit is it?
Ounce: Unit of mass. The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.
He earned a PhD in physics from Cambridge for the first-ever thesis on quantum mechanics, then shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?

There are exactly five of these convex regular polyhedra — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron — named for the philosopher who linked them to the classical elements. What are they called?
Platonic solid: Any of the five regular polyhedra. In geometry, a Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
This legal document spells out how a business collects, stores, and shares personal details like your address, financial records, or medical history — what is it called?
Privacy policy: Management of personal data across media.
Recognizable by its bold red-and-black pattern, this true bug is often confused with the unrelated cinnamon bug and forms large aggregations across Europe and Asia — which species is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus: Species of true bug. The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
Scholars call it an "essentially contested concept" with no agreed definition, but it broadly links humanity to the supernatural through behaviors, ethics, texts and sacred places — what is it?

Nicknamed the 'dark lady of DNA,' this X-ray crystallographer's crucial contributions to the discovery of DNA's structure went largely unrecognized in her lifetime — James Watson believed she'd have won a Nobel Prize had she lived. Who was she?
Also called Besnier–Boeck–Schaumann disease, this non-infectious condition forms clusters of inflammatory cells called granulomata, often starting in the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes — what is it?
Sarcoidosis: Abnormal formation of clumps of inflammatory cells (granulomata)
A slender African cat with a tiny head and enormous ears, this golden, black-spotted hunter is the sole member of its genus and stands tall on remarkably long legs — which wild cat is it?
Known commonly as baking soda, this white crystalline compound with the formula NaHCO3 occurs naturally as the mineral nahcolite — what is its chemical name?
Sodium bicarbonate: Chemical compound. It is a salt composed of a sodium cation (Na+) and a bicarbonate anion (HCO−3).
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Also called the broadbill, this large migratory predator sports a long, flat, pointed bill and can reach nearly 15 feet in length — what fish is it?
Swordfish: Fish which has a long, pointed bill. Swordfish are elongated, round-bodied, and lose all teeth and scales by adulthood.

Believing he'd been commanded to build the biblical Third Temple, this engineer single-handedly created an operating system written in a language he invented himself, despite later struggles with schizophrenia and homelessness — who was he?
Terry A. Davis: American computer programmer (1969–2018)
With the symbol Sn and atomic number 50, this metal emits a crackling 'cry' when bent and boasts more stable isotopes than any other element — which one?
Tin: Chemical element with atomic number 50 (Sn). A metallic-gray metal, tin is soft enough to be cut with little force, and a bar of tin can be bent by hand with little effort.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
Found only in the northern Gulf of California, this porpoise is the smallest living cetacean and is critically endangered due to bycatch from an illegal fishery — which species?
Vaquita: Endangered species of porpoise. The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.

Known for quoting multiple religious scriptures in English lectures delivered in a suit and tie rather than traditional robes, this Indian preacher had his foundation banned in 2016 amid hate-speech and money-laundering accusations. Who is he?
The symbol for calcium is Ca. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
The symbol for thorium is Th. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.

Barbra Streisand: Barbara Joan "Barbra" Streisand ( STRY-sand; born April 24, 1942) is an American singer, actress, songwriter, and filmmaker.

Courteney Cox: Courteney Bass Cox (born June 15, 1964) is an American actress and producer.

Suzanne Somers: Suzanne Marie Somers (née Mahoney; October 16, 1946 – October 15, 2023) was an American actress, author, and businesswoman.
